$comment: Phase 5, section 9. Budgets are the measurements below plus a margin, not rounded down to look tight. `scripts/perf-gate.mjs` checks cold start and the two snapshot sizes on a seeded database (200 conversations, 2,000 messages); apps/desktop/src/ui/perf.mounted.test.tsx checks renderMs. Every check is the median of 3 runs, because CI machines vary. Raising a number here is a decision that needs a reason in the commit message.
$measured: 2026-10-31, Lane D worktree at 71c857f, Windows 10, debug build (cargo build, as CI builds it), seeded with 200 conversations and 2,000 messages: cold start median 567 ms (first run on a cold file cache 1,933 ms), app.snapshot 1,060,106 bytes, lazy 452,586 bytes (42.7% of full). renderMs: a 1,000-message conversation mounted in happy-dom on a quiet machine took 4,534, 8,038 and 14,552 ms (median 8,038 ms), and 19 to 30 s while Rust was compiling. It rises from run to run, which needs looking at. So this budget is a regression alarm for a slow test DOM, not a target for the real app, whose time in WebView2 hasn't been measured.
